title: DevFolio (FolioHub)
summary: A social platform where developers post portfolio projects and get rated on UI, UX and code quality.
story: I wanted a place where developers could get real feedback on their portfolios instead of guessing whether a project actually reads well to a hiring manager. DevFolio lets you submit a project as versioned iterations (screenshots, a live URL and notes per revision) and put it in front of a community that rates it on UI, UX and code quality. It grew into more than a feedback board: likes, comments, longer-form community 'roasts', a leaderboard and top-stack rankings, plus an AI Studio that generates a structured, scored review you can share. It is the tool I wished existed the first time I was not sure if my portfolio was actually any good.
built: Go and Gin power the API with GORM against a PostgreSQL database on Neon, JWT auth via golang-jwt, and Swagger docs generated with swaggo. The frontend is SvelteKit on Svelte 5 with TypeScript and Tailwind CSS 4, styled with Phosphor Icons and mdsvex for content. AI Studio calls Groq's OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint (openai/gpt-oss-120b) to generate structured, scored reviews and roasts. Tests run through Vitest with vitest-browser-svelte and Playwright for end-to-end coverage, linted with ESLint and formatted with Prettier.

title: SnipStack
summary: A snippet and prompt manager for developers and AI coding agents, with a personal style profile agents can read to match your conventions.
story: I kept losing good snippets and prompts across projects, and re-explaining my conventions to every new AI coding session got old fast. SnipStack is where I save and organize code snippets and prompts alongside a personal 'style profile' that agents can read to match how I actually write code. It has a social layer on top (collections, tags, follows, stars, comments and a trending feed), so it is not just a private vault. The part I am most proud of is the agent-integration story: a REST API with scoped API keys and a dedicated MCP server, so Claude, Gemini or any MCP-capable agent can search, fetch and fork my snippets and prompts mid-task instead of me copy-pasting them in.
built: Go's net/http serves the API with GORM against PostgreSQL, JWT sessions, GitHub OAuth alongside email/password auth, and OpenAPI/Swagger docs. The frontend is Next.js 16 on the App Router with React 19, TanStack Query, React Hook Form and Zod for forms, Tailwind CSS and shadcn/ui for the interface, Recharts for stats and next-themes for dark mode. Agent access runs through the official MCP SDK. Local development runs on Docker Compose, with production configs for Render and Fly.io on the backend and a standalone Docker image or Vercel/Netlify for the frontend.

title: 2026 Christmas
summary: A festive single-page holiday greeting with playful animated 'gift' pages you're meant to click through and share.
story: I wanted a holiday card that was actually fun to open instead of another static 'Merry Christmas' image. 2026 Christmas greets visitors with an animated message, then lets them pick a gift: a 'Mystery Gift' page that redirects to a random YouTube video after three clicks, or a 'Money' page that jokingly refuses to give anything and lectures you about the value of giving instead. The homepage also throws in a randomized fake SIM-credit giveaway card just for the joke. It leans fully into being a shareable, animation-heavy holiday toy rather than a serious utility.
built: Built with Next.js App Router and TypeScript, styled with Tailwind CSS and shadcn-style primitives (a Card component built on class-variance-authority, clsx and tailwind-merge). Framer Motion drives the page transitions and gift interactions, react-snowfall renders the falling snow, and Lucide React supplies the icons. Fonts load through next/font with Google's Mountains of Christmas and Roboto alongside Geist. Deployed live on Vercel.

title: Solaris
summary: A marketing site for an Ethiopian electric Bajaj/Tuk-Tuk mobility company, with an interactive 3D globe highlighting Ethiopia and dedicated investor and supplier lead pages.
story: Solaris is a marketing site I built for an electric Bajaj/Tuk-Tuk mobility company entering the Ethiopian market. It presents the product and the financing and battery-swap ecosystem around it, plus dedicated pages for investors and component suppliers, each with its own contact form. The homepage carries an interactive About accordion, a product showcase with a battery-swap 'switching' animation, a performance section, and an interactive 3D globe that plots the world's landmass as a dot field and pulses a marker over Ethiopia. It is the most visually ambitious site I have shipped. Getting the globe to feel alive without tanking performance took real tuning.
built: Next.js 16 on the App Router with Turbopack, React 19 and TypeScript, styled with Tailwind CSS 4 and shadcn/ui built on Radix UI primitives, with next-themes for dark mode, Lucide, Hugeicons and Font Awesome for icons, and react-fast-marquee for scrolling strips. The globe is Three.js via React Three Fiber and drei, with a custom GLSL shader through React Three Postprocessing for its glow ring. Linted with ESLint and formatted with Prettier (prettier-plugin-tailwindcss), styling utilities via class-variance-authority, clsx and tailwind-merge.

title: Prime Capital
summary: The corporate marketing site for an Ethiopian securities and investment firm, with live market prices, multilingual news, and vacancy listings pulled from a remote CMS.
story: Prime Capital is the corporate site I built for an Ethiopian securities and investment firm, presenting their market data, listed companies, news, team, and job openings to the public. The homepage carries a hero slider and a live market-prices ticker, and visitors can read blog and news posts in English, Amharic and Oromo, meet the leadership team, and browse and apply to open vacancies filtered by level and employment period. News and job data come from the firm's own REST API and are fetched and cached client-side, while the rest of the site is static Next.js pages. It is the most content-heavy site I have built. Getting multilingual CMS content to render cleanly across pages took the most care.
built: Next.js 16 on the App Router with React 19 and TypeScript, styled with Tailwind CSS 4, Radix UI primitives (accordion, avatar, dialog, dropdown menu, select, separator) and shadcn-style components. Framer Motion (Motion) drives animation, Lottie renders an animated business icon, react-youtube embeds video, and Heroicons plus Lucide/React Icons cover iconography, with next-themes for theming. News and vacancy data is fetched from the firm's REST API through Axios and cached with TanStack React Query (React Query Devtools in development). Linted with ESLint's flat config (eslint-config-next), styling utilities via PostCSS/Autoprefixer, clsx and tailwind-merge.

title: Flowery Invitation
summary: A single-page digital invitation for a corporate partner welcome event, with RSVP via Google Forms and a loading screen that waits for the background photo.
story: I built this as a single-page digital invitation for Pitron Technology Solutions PLC, inviting the Temenos team to a partner welcome event in Addis Ababa. It presents the date, time, venue and dress code over a decorative floral visual layer, and lets guests RSVP through an embedded Google Form, with connection pre-warming and prefetching so that external hop feels instant. A custom loading screen holds the page behind a spinner until the Cloudinary-hosted background photo has fully loaded, so the invitation always reveals itself against a finished backdrop rather than a half-loaded image. It shipped as its own containerized Next.js app rather than a page bolted onto an existing site.
built: Next.js 16 on the App Router with React 19 and TypeScript, styled with Tailwind CSS 4 and shadcn/ui (base-nova style) on Base UI primitives, lucide-react for icons, class-variance-authority and tailwind-merge for styling utilities, and next/font loading DM Sans, Libre Franklin and Caveat from Google Fonts. Packaged with a multi-stage Dockerfile on Node 22-alpine using Next.js's standalone output for containerized deployment, linted with ESLint. RSVPs go through an embedded Google Form, and the background photo is served from Cloudinary.

title: Node Solutions
summary: A multi-page marketing site for a company with four service lines, featuring a filterable project portfolio, a validated contact form, and an on-demand PDF portfolio download.
story: Node Solutions is a marketing site I am building for a company with four service lines (digital marketing, creative printing, interior design & construction, and networking/IT solutions) laid out across dedicated home, about, services, projects and contact pages. It has an animated hero slideshow, a filterable project portfolio with detail pages, and a service-interest contact form validated with React Hook Form and Zod that posts to a server action. A companion API route generates a downloadable PDF portfolio on demand with pdf-lib, and the UI has light/dark theming, toast notifications and a confetti flourish on submission. It is still in active development. Form submissions and the generated PDF are currently placeholder output rather than wired up to a CMS or database.
built: Next.js 16 on the App Router with React 19 and TypeScript, styled with Tailwind CSS 4 and hand-rolled shadcn/ui primitives configured through components.json. Forms run on React Hook Form with Zod validation via @hookform/resolvers and submit through Next.js Server Actions; a Route Handler at app/api/contact and another at app/api/portfolio/download generate a PDF with pdf-lib on demand. Framer Motion and Lottie (lottie-react) drive animation, canvas-confetti fires on successful submission, next-themes handles light/dark mode, and Lucide supplies icons. Linted with ESLint and formatted with Prettier (prettier-plugin-tailwindcss).

title: Yehulu Wallet
summary: A multi-page marketing site for a digital wallet product, built around a scroll-driven SVG hero animation and a custom cursor and page-transition system.
story: Yehulu Wallet's marketing site pitches a digital wallet product (instant transfers, crypto support, international payments, and mini-apps) across a home page and supporting pricing, FAQ, team, about, blog and contact pages. I ported it from an HTML/CSS animation template to Next.js App Router, keeping the custom scroll-driven hero animation (HeroMorph) that morphs an SVG through interpolated geometry as you scroll, along with a global custom cursor and shared page-transition chrome. It is a static, content-first site with no backend: the contact form renders but does not submit anywhere yet, and there is no data fetching or environment config in the app. It is still actively being iterated on rather than a finished, deployed product.
built: Next.js 16 on the App Router with React 19 and TypeScript, styled with Tailwind CSS v4 and Manrope loaded through next/font. The scroll, cursor and page-transition effects run on ported template assets (libs.min.js, app.js, and custom hero-theme.css/main.css) carried over from the original HTML/CSS template rather than rebuilt as React state. Linted with ESLint 9 (eslint-config-next).

title: Nobel Lemat
summary: A marketing site for a logistics and transportation company, presenting fleet management, mobile delivery and security & cleaning services with a jQuery/Bootstrap-era animation stack ported into Next.js.
story: Nobel Lemat's site presents a logistics and transportation company's fleet management, mobile delivery, and security & cleaning service lines alongside a company overview, careers page, and contact form. Each route is a thin Next.js App Router page that reads pre-built HTML fragments from a local content directory and injects them into the DOM, so page copy can be edited independently of the React shell. All the client-side interactivity (sliders, counters, lightboxes, scroll animations, date pickers) runs on a jQuery/Bootstrap-era asset bundle loaded globally through the root layout instead of React components. It is built for straightforward content delivery and SEO-friendly per-page metadata rather than dynamic app behavior.
built: Next.js App Router with React and TypeScript for routing and per-page metadata, with page content sourced from static HTML fragments in a content/ directory. Styling and interactivity run on Bootstrap and jQuery, with Slick and Swiper for carousels, GSAP and ScrollTrigger for scroll animation, fancyBox for lightboxes, WOW.js for reveal-on-scroll effects, and nice-select and daterangepicker for form controls. Linted with ESLint.

title: Mereb Landing
summary: The marketing and API documentation site for a payment gateway product, backed by a headless Strapi CMS and a bilingual SACCO loan-repayment flow that proxies a real backend.
story: Mereb Landing is the marketing and documentation site for Mereb Gateway, a payment gateway product. It covers the usual marketing pages (home, about, services, case studies, developers, blog, contact) plus an interactive API documentation section at /docs covering guides, webhooks and error handling. Content is sourced from a companion Strapi CMS with ISR and webhook-driven revalidation, falling back to static local data if Strapi is unreachable. It also hosts a bilingual English/Amharic SACCO loan-repayment flow that proxies a real backend API for account lookup and payment-link creation, and collects contact and newsletter submissions straight into Strapi.
built: Next.js 16 on the App Router with React 19 and TypeScript, styled with Tailwind CSS v4 and Radix UI primitives (accordion, dialog, dropdown menu, navigation menu), with a custom cookie-based i18n layer for English/Amharic. Route Handlers cover contact and newsletter submission, CMS revalidation webhooks, and SACCO loan-repayment proxying through a shared-secret-gated integration with the SACCO's public API. Content comes from a separate Strapi v5 instance over HTTP rather than a database in this app. Packaged with Docker's standalone Next.js build, linted with ESLint.

title: Capsule
summary: A mobile app for writing a note to your future self, sealing it with attachments until a chosen date, and unlocking it automatically with a local notification.
story: Capsule is a mobile app for writing a note to your future self, attaching photos or files, and sealing it until a chosen open date. Once sealed, a capsule is locked from editing, export, or early reading, even by its own author, and unlocks automatically with a local notification when its open day arrives. All data stays on-device with no account or cloud sync, and a PIN plus biometric authentication protects sealing and opening capsules. It is built for one person's private, delayed-delivery notes rather than sharing or collaboration.
built: Flutter and Dart with Material widgets, custom design tokens, and a rich-text note editor and controller. Capsules are stored in SQLite through sqflite on mobile and sqflite_common_ffi on desktop, with path and path_provider handling file and database paths. local_auth gates sealing and opening with Face ID or fingerprint, flutter_local_notifications with timezone schedules the unlock notification for each capsule's open date, permission_handler manages runtime permissions, and file_selector handles attaching photos and files.

title: PlantPal
summary: A plant-care companion for Android that identifies houseplants from a photo, generates an AI care schedule, and tracks garden health over time.
story: PlantPal is a plant-care companion for Android that lets users identify houseplants from a photo, get an AI-generated care schedule, and track their garden's health over time. I built the backend as a Go REST API that uses Google Gemini (with Groq and OpenRouter as no-billing fallback providers) for plant identification and a conversational AI diagnosis chat for disease symptoms, backed by a Postgres database via GORM and Cloudinary for photo storage. The Flutter client covers plant collection management, recurring care reminders (watering, fertilizing, misting, rotation) with push and local notifications, a growth and photo journal, garden-wide health scoring, weather context via Open-Meteo, and a community feed with posts, comments and likes. Because the app runs on a stripped-down Flutter SDK without plugin support, I hand-rolled the native Android integrations (camera/photo picker, notifications, FCM push, Google Sign-In, and deep links) as Kotlin MethodChannel bridges instead of relying on federated plugins.
built: Go with Gorilla Mux and GORM against PostgreSQL, JWT auth (golang-jwt) with a short-lived access token and a longer-lived single-use refresh token, plus a Google Sign-In flow. Google Gemini (generative-ai-go) handles plant identification and the diagnosis chat, with Groq and OpenRouter as no-billing fallback providers, Firebase Admin SDK for push notifications and Google auth, Cloudinary for photo storage, golang.org/x/time for rate limiting, and a full Swagger/OpenAPI spec via swaggo for client generation. The Flutter client talks to it over the http package, hand-rolls the native Android integrations as Kotlin MethodChannel bridges (camera/photo picker, notifications, FCM push, Google Sign-In, deep links), uses path_provider for local persistence, lucide_icons_flutter for iconography, and ValueNotifier for lightweight state management. Deployed with Docker, with weather context pulled from Open-Meteo.

title: Linksy (Qontact)
summary: A mobile app for sharing your phone number and social profiles as a scannable QR code, and scanning others' codes to instantly save a contact or open a link.
story: Linksy is a mobile app built with Expo and React Native that lets people share their phone number, Telegram, or Twitter/X profile as a scannable QR code, and scan QR codes from others to instantly save a contact or open a link. Users enter their numbers and social links once in a 'Configure' screen; the app generates vCard/MECARD-style QR codes for sharing and parses incoming QR payloads (vCard, MECARD, tel/sms/mailto URIs), surfacing actionable results like 'Add to Contacts' or 'Open link.' On Android it can also read phone numbers directly off the device's SIM slots through a custom native Expo module. All data (contacts, links, and onboarding state) stays on-device in AsyncStorage; nothing is sent to a server.
built: React Native 0.81 (New Architecture) with Expo SDK 54 and Expo Router (typed routes), styled with NativeWind/Tailwind CSS. Forms run on React Hook Form with Zod validation, TanStack React Query handles data fetching and caching, and react-native-reusables (built on @rn-primitives/*) supplies accessible components like alert dialogs, select and label. QR codes are generated with react-native-qrcode-svg and scanned with expo-camera, expo-contacts writes to device contacts, sonner-native handles toasts, and icons come from lucide-react-native and Feather. On Android, a custom local Expo native module (modules/sim-numbers) reads SIM carrier and number info through expo-modules-core. Persistence is local-only via @react-native-async-storage/async-storage, with no database. Built and shipped with EAS Build/Submit for Android and iOS, TypeScript throughout, and Prettier with the Tailwind plugin.

title: Poster Boi (Watermark Bot)
summary: A Telegram bot that rewrites user text with Gemini in a chosen tone and automatically watermarks every post in a registered channel.
story: Poster Boi is a Telegram bot that refines user-submitted text and automatically watermarks channel posts. Users set preferences (grammar correction, funny tone, professional tone) and send text via /post, which the bot sends to Google's Gemini API for rewriting before returning the polished result. Separately, /watermark lets a user register a Telegram channel, by forwarding a message or supplying its username, and save a signature text that the bot appends to every subsequent post in that channel by editing the message after it's published.
built: Runs as a Cloudflare Worker written in TypeScript, handling Telegram updates via webhook rather than long-polling, using Telegraf for the Telegram Bot API and the Google GenAI SDK for Gemini-powered rewriting. User preferences, channels and watermarks are persisted in a PostgreSQL database through Prisma, using its Cloudflare runtime client with @prisma/adapter-pg. Deployed and developed with Wrangler, dotenv for configuration, and a tsx script for webhook registration.

title: Nati-Vim
summary: A personal Neovim configuration built on LazyVim, with a custom startup dashboard, curated language support, and colorschemes that hot-reload with the OS theme.
story: Nati-Vim is my personal Neovim configuration, built on top of LazyVim and kept in a dedicated dotfiles-style repo mirroring my active ~/.config/nvim setup. It layers a custom 'Nati-Vim' startup dashboard, curated language support (TypeScript, Go, Rust, Dart, HTML/CSS), and a set of hand-picked plugins for file navigation, formatting, and quick file-jumping on top of LazyVim's defaults. It integrates with Omarchy's theme system so the colorscheme hot-reloads across around 20 bundled themes whenever the OS theme changes, and includes an OSC 52-based clipboard that works transparently over SSH and tmux. It is built for my own day-to-day editing workflow across web, Go, and Rust projects.
built: Neovim configured in Lua, built on lazy.nvim for plugin management with LazyVim as the base distribution. LSP, completion, formatting and linting run through Treesitter, nvim-lspconfig, mason.nvim/mason-lspconfig.nvim, blink.cmp, conform.nvim and nvim-lint. Editor UI and UX come from neo-tree.nvim, grapple.nvim, flash.nvim, mini.nvim (align, ai, icons, pairs), bufferline.nvim, noice.nvim, gitsigns.nvim, trouble.nvim and persistence.nvim, with snacks.nvim covering the dashboard, picker and scrolling. rustaceanvim and crates.nvim handle Rust, and nvim-ts-autotag covers HTML/CSS. Around 20 bundled colorschemes (Tokyonight, Gruvbox, Kanagawa and others) are wired to Omarchy's theme system for live hot-reload, and StyLua formats the Lua config itself.
